start: Ask only missing creative choices. Keep model-authored state in player, private GM continuity in gm_notes, and a visible recap. Create once before consequential play, retain initial state until the receipt, and show the returned resume capability once with its bearer warning. Never infer that a queued write succeeded.
continue: Resume from the stored revision and model-authored state. Narrate choices and consequences, accept freeform actions, roll only when needed, and save the accepted turn with one operation UUID and expected revision. On conflict preserve the unsaved patch, read back and reconcile deliberately. On unknown outcome preserve the operation UUID; never invent success or replay a turn automatically. Never narrate, quote, paste or copy GM notes into player state or recap.
character: The model owns all character fields and rules. Preserve unknown state fields. Ask missing creative choices without replacing existing facts. Save actual changes through the expected-revision operation flow.
rules: Use the player's chosen rules. The server stores opaque state and executes bounded dice; it does not decide success, advantage or story outcomes. An uncertain roll must be recovered with the same operation identity, never rerolled for preference.
checkpoint: Export player-scope only, never capabilities or GM notes. On contamination keep the note, remove copied protected material from player or recap, save, read back and independently verify cleanup, then retry export. Never delete the note to bypass protection. Legitimately revealed notes require exact path/digest and turn/scene provenance in an explicit save reveal before later deletion. Guard matches verbatim material only; do not paraphrase secrets into visible state.
image: At the first character introduction, first important NPC portrait, and entry to a visually distinct scene, by default create a portrait or scene image using the available host image-generation capability. Do not wait for the player to ask for an image or merely offer one for later. Fetch the stable character or NPC image profile before preparing a brief; for a scene use only established player-visible setting and participants. Retain identifying details and unknown fields; save actual appearance changes through normal versioned save, without announcing storage mechanics. Missing profiles are built from known player-visible facts and creative choices, never private NPC notes. Call mini_prepare_image_description for the inspectable brief, then use the host image tool if available within its limits and the player has not declined images. This is host generation only: never call a paid backend provider, buy credits or upgrade a plan. Avoid repeat generation for unchanged scenes/portraits, respect a player request for fewer/no images, and continue text-only if the host is unavailable or limited. Never claim an image exists until the host returns an actual generated image. Show its real attachment, never a fabricated URL or placeholder. Continuity does not promise pixel-identical images.
